content.comment_body: Hello, I have a problem. I need to create a program that can control a frequency converter, but I'm not sure how to do this on a computer. I don't just want to monitor if the frequency converter is on or off—I want to select any frequency between 0 and 2000 Hz. This is for a project, so I need to demonstrate this works using a computer. Any help or ideas?

There isn't a universal program for controlling a frequency converter. Without more specific information, it will be difficult to assist you. You mentioned setting the frequency between 0 and 2000 Hz?

Do you think you can help me if I give you the reference of the frequency converter? And about choosing between 0 and 2000 Hz, I meant being able to select values like 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, or 10 Hz, etc. I'm French, so sorry for my English.

We have no details from you. Which [product_name] do you use exactly? Please also provide the complete order number. Maybe sharing a link to the converter manual could help. But it's impossible to assist with no information.
You're right, it's the [product_name] [version_no], and this is a beta. I don't know what else I can tell that might help you assist me. Other than that, I don't have more to provide.
If you can't specify which [product_name] you have (I'm not familiar with a beta), and can't identify the frequency converter, then I can't help. As mentioned, there’s no universal solution.
Can values be changed using the [product_name] software on the device if there is a screen? Would that information be useful for you? This is my only issue. I found the version—it's [version_no].
No, none of that information helps.

Let me try to explain again. My problem is I can't program control for any equipment to select, for example, on an interface, a value like 100, 6, or 600, or some other value. Is it possible to create such a program?
Sorry, I don't understand what you want to do.

The motor drive should be able to adjust speed using the built-in knob or screen. It may also be possible to connect a variable resistor or potentiometer directly to the drive. Some speed adjustment might be possible from the [product_name], with several options: 1) Analog setpoint to the drive, 2) Up/Down speed via digital outputs, 3) Modbus TCP communications, 4) Combination outputs selecting presets in the drive. There are many approaches, but volunteers need details about your actual devices. Setting a speed of "2000 Hz" seems unusually high, which makes it hard to understand your requirements. Sharing your application needs is crucial for effective help. Volunteers can guide you, but will not carry out the entire project for you. If you need extensive assistance, you might want to consider hiring a contractor.

Hello, I'll try one last time. I think I'll try working alone. I'm on the computer version of [product_name] V8.3. I don't have the API yet and I want to create a program that lets me change information—for example you can see it in the screenshot. Can I increase or decrease the value of a threshold detector (from, say, 45 to 60 for off) directly on the API via an interface? Sorry if I'm disturbing you.
You mean you're using the demo version of [product_name] V8.3?
Yes, that's it.
You're not disturbing anyone. But it's challenging—almost impossible—since you haven't explained what you're actually doing. Or is this just a learning exercise?

It's not a learning exercise, it's a second-year project for a degree (I'm not sure if that's called the same elsewhere). I need to show that my project works in theory, so I'm trying to change a value in a program with the API, and see if it can be simulated in [product_name] [product_name] software. My question: does your API allow changing, for example, a speed value with buttons on the API? I will program it myself, but just want to know if this is possible. The goal: I have a project to create a testing bench for overspeed triggers with 2 sensors (temperature and speed). I want to build a program that would, for example, run a motor at a requested speed, and then, after reaching a certain temperature, increase to a specified speed at a given number of rpm. Sorry for the formatting—it's so you can read everything without missing details. Thank you.

Which "API" are you referring to? I'm confused when something is posted and there's no context. If my guess is correct, you're looking for a setpoint adjuster whose value can be changed using the buttons on the [product_name] base module. Is that what you mean?
If my guess is correct, then the attached program might help you.
Thank you. That's what I needed.
Is it normal that when I open the file, it says it can't be opened?
If that's happening, the problem is with your PC. I downloaded the uploaded ZIP file, extracted it, and was able to load the file using [product_name] software.
I succeeded, it works.
Thank you for your patience.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is struggling to design a program that would allow them to control a frequency converter and select any frequency value within a broad range via a user interface, using [product_name] hardware and software ([version_no]). Uncertainty about whether the [product_name] system and software can communicate with a frequency converter in the desired way, and how to set or adjust values, is the main user experience challenge. Lack of complete details and language differences further complicate communication with those trying to help.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to be able to program frequency control—specifically to choose any value from 0 to 2000 Hz—using the [product_name] system and software, ideally via a user interface.
